chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Ḍurays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever carries a weapon at night is a muharib, unless he is a man who is not among the people of suspicion.

key_terms.الرِّيبَةِ: suspicion; doubtful or suspect character relevant to the ruling
key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: weapon; the carried armament mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: at night; the circumstance in which this act is judged
key_terms.رَجُلًا: a man; the individual excepted in the statement
key_terms.مُحَارِبٌ: one deemed to be in a state of armed hostility or violent threat

ai.seo_question: When is carrying a weapon at night considered muharabah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who carries weapons at night, treating such conduct as an act associated with hostile threat and public danger. It makes an exception for a person who is not regarded as suspicious, indicating that surrounding circumstances and reputation are relevant in applying the ruling.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5124 - Ali ibn Ri'ab narrated from Ḍurays from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "
Whoever carries a weapon at night is considered a highway robber (muharib), unless he is a man who is not known for suspicion or wrongdoing."
